subject.title: Feature: Per-spawn tool restrictions for sub-agents

question: Should OpenClaw expose per-spawn `sessions_spawn` tool restrictions as the open candidate PR's allow-only `toolsAllow` API, or require a broader allow/deny policy shape before landing?
rationale: The implementation boundary is clear, but the public API shape affects security guarantees, compatibility, stored child-session policy, and unsupported-runtime failure behavior.

options.title: Land Allowlist-First API
options.body: Accept `toolsAllow` as the additive first contract, with documented empty-list behavior and fail-closed unsupported-runtime handling.

options.title: Require Allow/Deny Policy
options.body: Hold the candidate until the API supports both allow and deny semantics matching the original least-privilege proposal more directly.

options.title: Defer Broader Design
options.body: Keep the issue open while maintainers design a larger delegated tool-policy model across spawned sessions, route bindings, cron, and related APIs.

recommendation.title: Land Allowlist-First API
recommendation.body: Accept `toolsAllow` as the additive first contract, with documented empty-list behavior and fail-closed unsupported-runtime handling.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter is tied to the original `sessions_spawn` feature and later security-adjacent hardening on this surface.
